newsitem.title: DENMARK: SAS Cargo turnover six percent up in 1996.
newsitem.headline: SAS Cargo turnover six percent up in 1996.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) cargo division said in an annual report document on Wednesday that freight turnover rose six percent in 1996 from the previous year.
This put 1996 cargo earnings at 1.8 billion Swedish crowns compared to the previous year's 1.7 billion Swedish crowns.

It said total freight and post traffic rose 33 percent to 668.5 million tonnes per kilometre in 1996 from 1995's 502.3 million, with the increased activity mainly attributable to intercontinental cargo operations, which were 43 percent up last year at 561.8 million tonnes per kilometre.
This meant that intercontinental cargo activity represented about 85 percent of SAS' total freight and post traffic, it said.
SAS Cargo head Peter Groenlund told Reuters he foresaw positive growth after business picked up in February and March following a sluggish January.
SAS on Tuesday removed a cargo fuel surcharge introduced last November, but Groenlund warned that new rate rises were possible in a sector in which competition was fierce.
SAS Cargo entered agreements last year to combine freight operations with ally Lufthansa and United Airlines. --Soeren Linding Jakobsen, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969653
